speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) how many Silver Generation Office ambassadors and staff are currently engaged in outreach activities; and (b) in each of the last three years, how many (i) home visits and (ii) telephone check-ins have been conducted.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I think a lot has been raised in this House of the concerns for the mental wellness of our elderly.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: As the COVID-19 pandemic drags on, it has been quite a while since some of them have had house visits.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Can the Ministry also talk about the forward-looking plans?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Will we bring the house visits back to the level of about 300,000 and when will that happen?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Indeed, the COVID-19 pandemic has caused a shift in the way SGO reaches out to these seniors.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To move forward, we also need to understand the genesis of the SGO.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: When it then evolved in April 2019 to merge with AIC, the expanded scope was then to reach out to another bigger group.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, initially, it was a smaller group; and it extended to a bigger group.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In 2020, SGO then had to adjust and pivot, to shift into doing house visits as well as tele-engagements with the vulnerable group.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And this is also something that we need to continue looking at.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I understand the concerns because the elderly are at home and they are not able to engage.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are also enhancing the competency of the SGAs to engage our seniors more effectively, so that they can continue to stay active and mentally engaged as well.
